Commentary.Commentary: A good bowling performance from New Zealand but again, they failed to capitalize on a good start. In both innings they had India in trouble but a couple of good partnerships swung the momentum. It is now upto their batsmen to try and fight hard. 376 is the target but they will try and look at it as trying to play out 5-and-a-half sessions. Their first aim would be to see off this hour's play without losing a wicket. Stay tuned for their reply.

So then it has taken around 13 overs this morning to take the remaining two wickets. Guess the runs today would not matter too much as the Kiwis were already in troubled waters after the Rohit-Saha partnership. Boult got himself into the wickets column with 3 scalps in the second innings.

OUT! THAT IS IT! Good length ball around the off stump channel, Shami tries to defend but gets a thick outside edge. The ball flies towards gully where Latham takes a good low catch. The Kiwi fielders are not sure though but Latham appeals for the catch. The umpire refers it upstairs but his soft signal is out. Replays aren't clear but Simon Doull on air feels it has carried. The third umpire takes his time and gives it out, going with the soft signal as he doesn't have enough evidence to rule it not out. India are bowled out! NEW ZEALAND NEED 376 RUNS TO WIN!

Hello everyone to the coverage of the day 4 of the second Test between India and New Zealand in Kolkata. The hosts are in a comfortable position with a strong lead of 339 runs and have still two wickets left.
...Day 4, Session 1...

New Zealand fought hard but still find themselves in a very tough situation as India are ahead by 339 runs with two wickets still remaining. The hosts might look to bat for an hour tomorrow and swell the lead even more. New Zealand need an inspirational performance to fight from this scenario but you can expect them to give some magical moments for us. Join us back then tomorrow at 0915 IST to catch the day 4 action. Until then, goodbye and take care. Cheers!

Earlier in the day, Jeetan Patel did well to take their total past the 200-run mark. Shami cleaned up their lower order and finished with three wickets. In reply, India lost early wickets and were reduced to 43/4 at one stage. Trent Boult and Matt Henry bowled well to take those wickets but Virat Kohli counter-attacked. His innings was cut short too but Rohit Sharma rose to the occasion at his favourite venue and put India in a commanding position in the end. He would be gutted though as he missed out on a deserving ton. Saha scored some handy runs too as he hit an unbeaten 39. In the end, they are in the driver's seat now and dictating terms.

Exciting day of Test cricket comes to an end! India will go back happily as they have a lead of 339 runs on the board. Rohit Sharma was brilliant with the bat as he played a superb knock under circumstances. India were in a spot of bother at one stage in this innings but they were never in trouble given the match situation.
It's gone really dark and the umpires take the reading and the light doesn't look enough. That should be it for the day then as the players walk back to the dressing room. STUMPS ON DAY 3!

Day 3, 3rd Session...

The pitch is acting up. Odd deliveries have misbehaved and it's enough to put doubts in the minds of the batsmen. India though are struggling at the moment, it's the Kiwis who will have a tough time batting last on this notorious track. Do join us in a short while for the last session...

It was an unfortunate dismissal for the Indian skipper as a ball from Boult stayed low and rapped him on the pads, while Ravichandran Ashwin failed to contribute with the bat. India are ahead in this Test but to take this game by the scruff of the neck, they will require their lower order to once again step up. The lead at the moment is 222 runs and they will hope to post at least 350 as a target.

Terrific session for New Zealand and had they not conceded a lead in excess of 100 runs, they would have been in the driver's seat. It was a brilliant bowling show by the Kiwis after lunch and once again Matt Henry led the pack. The Indian top order was dismantled in a flash and then the 48-run stand between Kohli and Rohit came.

However, replays show the ball hitting the pad first, then the inside edge. Good decision in the end. INDIA ARE EFFECTIVELY 218/6!

Outside off, pushed through point for a single.
Outside off, left alone.
Full again, pushed straight back. Martin Guptill gets across from short extra cover and fumbles. The ball goes behind and Rohit wants the single but Ashwin sends him back.
Full and outside off, pushed towards mid off.

IN THE AIR... SAFE! Full and outside off, Ravichandran comes forward to defend and the ball hits something on the pitch. A puff of dust emanates and the cherry hits the face of the bat and lobs to mid off. Does not carry.
Full and outside off, Ashwin looks to defend but gets a bottom edge which goes to the off side. Wagner stops to collect.
The ball has found the edge of the bat.

FOUR BYES! Unlucky for the keeper. Full and outside off, Rohit pushes at it and the ball moves away late. Lands just in front of Watling who is unable to stop it and parries it to the third man fence. 100 UP FOR INDIA!
Outside off, tapped to the off side for a quick run.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single.
On middle, flicked away for a single.
Fuller in length and outside off, it's driven off the front foot to covers.
Back of a length ball on off, punched to cover-point for a run.
Angles in a length ball around off, Ashwin gets behind the line in defense.
Lands it on a length and outside off, Rohit stays back and steers it through point for a single.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
The ball is too wide on the off side for the batsman to make any contact.
RAVICHANDRAN ASHWIN is the new batsman.

OUT! Kohli is adjudged lbw! Unlucky for the Indian skipper as it stayed low. After bowling a barrage of deliveries in the zone outside off, Boult changes his angle and sprints in from around the wicket. He angles in a length ball around off, Kohli tries to defend but it stays agonizingly low to go past the bottom part of his bat and hit him on the pads. Kohli is almost on his haunches, the bowler turns back to appeal and is all pumped up as the finger goes up. The impact also looked to be a shade outside off and it was a marginal call from the umpire. Big scores are refusing to come from the bat of Kohli. INDIA LEAD BY 203 RUNS!
Full in length and around off, Kohli watchfully gets behind the line and blocks it to the off side.
The batsman picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.
Another delivery angling away from the batsman, on a good length, Kohli lets it through.
This is ineffective stuff from Boult. Bowling in the channel outside off, but way wide to make the batsman play.
Good length delivery angling across the right-hander, Kohli allows it through to the keeper.
Bowls it from wide of the crease and delivers a length delivery outside off, Rohit takes his front leg forward before leaving it. He is showing a lot of patience by leaving these wide deliveries.
Good length delivery outside off, holding its line, Rohit has a very watchful leave.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fuller and on off, driven straight to the cover fielder.
Sprays a full ball wide outside off, Rohit allows it through.
Angles across a full length ball outside off, it's pushed off the front foot to covers.
The ball is too wide on the off side for the batsman to make any contact. End of a wayward over by Boult!
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Another delivery wide outside off and it's left alone by Kohli with ease.
Wide! The bowler completely loses control over his line and sprays a wild delivery outside off.
Full and outside off, Kohli works it on the leg side but straight to mid-wicket.

Lands it on a fuller length around middle and leg, Kohli gets behind the line and blocks it with a straight bat. Boult gets up in an appeal but then pulls out quickly. Maybe, he thought it was pad first and then bat. But in reality, it was the opposite.
Full in length and around off, Kohli gets forward and across to push it towards wide mid on.
TRENT BOULT is back on.
Brings a full ball back into the batsman this time, Kohli gets across the stumps, closes the face of the bat and helps it through mid-wicket for a run.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Wagner hurls in a very full ball and wide outside outside off, it's too wide to bother the Indian skipper.
Another delivery in the channel outside off, Kohli watchfully lets it through to the keeper.
A touch short and outside off, Kohli has nothing to do with it.
Good length ball outside off, Kohli chooses to leave it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, pushed towards point for a run.

FOUR! Excellent timing! Full on middle and off, Kohli just flicks it through mid-wicket. Initially it does not seem like there is much timing on it but once the ball goes in the gap, it races away. Substitute Doug Bracewell gives it a good chase and dives near the ropes but the ball wins. INDIA'S LEAD TOUCHES 200!

Full and outside off, Sharma lunges to open the face of the bat towards third man and gets a soft edge. The ball runs past first slip and third man mops it up. Once again, Kohli's running converts two into three. The stand is worth 41 from 38 balls.
Outside off, watchfully defended.

Flighted outside off, slowly bowled, Rohit lunges forward to defend but the ball beats the outside edge. In Patel's previous over, he beat Kohli with a quicker one. Now, he has beaten his partner with a slower one.
Outside off, left alone once again.
Full and outside off, well defended.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
Outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Crisp! The feeling of watching cricket gets brilliant when Kohli is elegant. Full on middle, Kohli comes half forward, just pushes the bat forward, meets the ball and the outfield does the rest. The cherry races away to the ropes. The lead is now 193.
Outside off, pushed through point for a single.

DRINKS BREAK. Action-packed session. New Zealand are winning hearts by giving it their everything. India have their noses in front but if the Kiwis keep picking up wickets, they might still stand a chance in the final innings.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Quicker one outside off, Virat lunges to defend but the ball goes past.
FOUR! Classy! What a shot. Flighted outside off, Kohli leans into it and drives it with ease through the covers for boundaries in succession! The stand is worth 33 from just 27 balls!

FOUR! Not where he intended to but he will get a boundary. Full and outside off, Kohli looks to flick but the ball takes the inner half of the bat and goes through square leg. The fielder from short fine runs after it but in vain. Kohli moves to 31.
Full and wide outside off, pushed through point for a single.

CLOSE CALL! Landed outside off, Rohit looks to push it to the off side but the ball takes the bottom edge, bounces behind, goes past the stumps, hits Watling on his left shoulder and goes to short leg.
Stays back in his crease and blocks.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
Way outside off, almost a reminiscence of his first innings dismissal, fuller in length, this time Kohli lets it be. Hallmark of a great player - learning from his mistakes and having a good memory.
The ball is way wide on the leg side but the batsman still goes after it.
WIDE. A short ball around off, Kohli goes for the pull but misses. Watling leaps to collect.
A length ball down the leg side, Kohli misses his flick.

FOUR! Up and over! If New Zealand are aggressive, India are counter-aggressive. They are tackling the short ball well now. This was outside off, Kohli stands tall and upper cuts it over the gully region to third man! The stand moves to 23 from 17 balls.
SIX! Creamed! That came out of nowhere. Flighted outside off, Rohit gets down and slog sweeps it over mid-wicket! Even Kohli was surprised and stuck his tongue out with a smile. The lead is now 174.
That stays low! Full and outside off, Rohit goes back to defend but the ball shoots low and the batsman just about keeps it out. Having said that, he should have been forward to that.

Ahem... it has been warnings and warnings for Virat Kohli in this Test series. In the first match, it was a warning for Jadeja running on the pitch. In this one too, a similar warning was given to the captain. And now, he himself has been warned for running on the pitch.
Pushes it towards point and takes a single.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
Outside off, well defended.
Full on middle, Kohli nudges it towards fine leg. That would have mostly been a single but the urgency shown by Kohli doubles the value.
JEETAN PATEL has been brought on.

An unofficial Drinks Break. This is not the first time it is happening in this Test. Conditions are really hot and humid and testing for the players. Even the umpires have helped themselves to a couple of water bottles in between.
Short and outside off, Kohli pulls it with a horizontal bat through mid on. Jeetan Patel lumbers after it from short mid-wicket and the batsmen get three when it should have been only two.
A short ball around middle and off, well kept out.
A length ball on middle, worked through mid-wicket for a run. The crowd cheers as the 50 is raised.
Another short ball, pulled to long leg for a single.
A short ball again, pulled through square leg for a couple.
A short ball around middle and leg, Kohli nudges it straight to Martin Guptill at leg gully.
Taylor wants more aggression. NEIL WAGNER comes on to bowl.
Outside off, pushed with an open face to point.
A sharp bouncer on middle, Rohit ducks.
Stays back in his crease and blocks.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. Two runs added to the total.
On middle, flicked away for a single.
ROHIT SHARMA walks in at number 6, replacing Rahane.

OUT! Gone! The short ball has consumed Rahane. Landed around off, Rahane goes for the pull but gets a top edge. The ball swirls in the air towards deep backward square leg. The man from short mid-wicket moves to his right but then Trent Boult comes running in from the deep, calls clearly and takes the catch with ease. Rahane is not happy with himself. India are in a spot of bother with their score reading 43/4 but add the 112-run lead and they are still in a comfortable position.
Full on middle and off, driven back to the bowler.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Landed outside off, left alone again.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
OUCH! That would have hurt. On a good length outside off, Rahane looks to defend but the ball jags back sharply and hits him on the bottom glove. Boult gives a stare to Rahane who stares back.
Full and outside off, well defended.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
FOUR! Almost an action replay of the previous boundary. Full and outside off, Kohli comes forward and drives it through the covers for a boundary!
Full on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Outside off, left alone this time.
FOUR! Classy! Full and outside off, Kohli comes forward, gets to the pitch of the ball and plays a punchy drive through the covers for a boundary! The lead touches 150 now.
On a good length around off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, left alone.
AJINKYA RAHANE, India's saviour in the first innings, walks out at number 5, replacing Dhawan. Not a dissimilar scenario to the one in the first innings.

OUT! LBW! India have lost their third wicket! Excellent bowling from Boult. Keeps this on a length targetting the stumps, Dhawan stays back to defend but is late in getting his bat down. He is hit on the pads and Boult appeals. The finger is up straightaway. INDIA ARE EFFECTIVELY 146/3!
A good short ball around off, watchfully kept out.
A short ball around the hips, Kohli pulls it disdainfully towards backward square leg for a single.
A bouncer now, Kohli ducks.
Outside off, angling away, left alone.
Shorter in length outside off, comes back in, SD sways away from the line.
Wider outside off, this time Shikhar lets it go.

FOUR! That was a bit streaky. Full and wide outside off, Dhawan leans to drive but he is not in control. The ball goes in the air behind point and is in the gap. Races to the fence. One thing is for sure - things will be happening now. You won't get a dull moment with these two in the middle.
A bouncer on middle, Dhawan ducks.
On middle and leg, Kohli works it behind square leg and gets three runs. The lead moves to 141.
Around middle and off, watchfully defended.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot for a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

Huge and massive appeal for LBW. Not out, says the umpire. On a length around leg, Kohli stays back to defend but misses. The ball stays low as well. Ross Taylor is frustrated but the replays make it clear in one go. PITCHED OUTSIDE LEG. Good decision.
Stays back in his crease and blocks it out again.
Full and outside off, defended watchfully.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
VIRAT KOHLI walks in now at number 4, replacing Pujara.

OUT! Pujara is adjudged lbw! Henry comes up with another full delivery which nips back into the batsman after landing around middle and off. Pujara this time fails to flick it on the leg side and is rapped on the pads. They appeal and the finger goes up this time. Well, that looked to be missing leg but umpire Kettleborough has other ideas. India in some early spot of bother!
Henry digs in a bouncer around off, Pujara ducks underneath it.

Appeal for an lbw! Henry gets one delivery to move into the batsman from a fuller length around off, Pujara this time fails to flick and is hit on the front pad. Appeal from the bowler and the keeper but the umpire shakes his head. Missing leg.
Back of a length delivery on off, Pujara is on the back foot as he defends it down safely.
FOUR! Excellent timing! Henry angles in a fuller length ball on middle, Pujara picks it off his pads and flicks it elegantly through mid-wicket for a boundary. A confidence booster for Che!
Played to the point region by the batsman. No run.
FOUR! Another good shot! Boult spears in a fuller length ball on middle, it's too straight in line and Dhawan leans across and forward to whip it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Dhawan lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Pitches it full and angles it into the batsman, Dhawan gets on the front foot and drives it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Shot! Width on offer outside off, a touch short as well, Dhawan camps back and cuts it powerfully through point for a cracking boundary.
Full length ball wide outside off, Dhawan has nothing to with it.

This is hostile stuff from Henry! Bangs in another sharp short ball on middle, Pujara is taken aback by the extra bounce, goes on the back foot, stands tall and then fends it off. But again we see Che taking his eyes off while doing all that. Not a good technique. It's a bit uppish but falls safely wide of short leg. End of a cracking over by Henry!

Boom! A great welcome delivery by Henry. He ups his pace and bangs in a lethal short delivery on off, Pujara takes his eyes off the ball and tries to duck. But he fails to move away from the line of fire and takes a blow on his chest. That would have hurt but he shows no pain.
CHETESHWAR PUJARA is the number 3 batsman.

OUT! Good low catch by Guptill! Henry hurls a length delivery around off and gets it to straighten a touch, Vijay could have left it alone but he has a needless push inside the line without any footwork. It takes the outside edge and flies towards second slip. The ball is dying in front of the fielder but Guptill does well to get down low and cups it safely with both hands. Murali is not very  happy with his attempted shot and walks back shaking his head.
Slower in pace this time, length and around off, Vijay remains in the comfort of his crease and defends it down.
Serves it on a length and outside off, Vijay pushes inside the line and plays it down off the outside half of the bat towards point.
Good positive intent first up shown by Henry. He delivers a shorter one but the line is not threatening. It's going down the leg side and Vijay shoulders arms to let it through to the keeper.
Welcome back. The players are striding out to the middle. Matt Henry to run in first up...
...DAY 3, SECOND SESSION...

India would probably look to bat the whole day now and it will be interesting to see how Dhawan bats. He's battling out hard as he took some blows and is looking out of form. Let's see how the Kiwis come back in the second session which is usually good for the batsmen. Join us back in a bit to catch the action!

Another good session for India! They managed to bowl out the Kiwis and then negotiated the tricky little period when they came out to bat. Shami did the damage with the ball today but that was after a handy knock by Jeetan Patel. India are sitting comfortably with a 124-run lead so far and have all their 10 wickets intact.
Full and down the leg side, Dhawan misses his flick and the ball goes off his pads. The fielder at leg gully dives to stop it. LUNCH ON DAY 3!
Will be the last ball before Lunch...
Down the leg side, nudged towards fine leg for a single.
Outside off, left alone.
Around a good length, middle and off, watchfully defended.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a couple.
Full and outside off, pushed towards gully.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Outside off, angling in, left alone.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.

FOUR! Caressed! That takes some courage. Full and outside off, Dhawan leans and drives it through the covers for a boundary! Excellent shot, considering that he has been hit on the thumb twice. The lead moves to 121.
Wider outside off, not played at.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
Down the leg side, SD looks to tuck it away but misses and is hit on the pads. The ball goes towards square leg and leg slip hurries to get to the ball but the single is completed. Leg bye taken.
Good length ball outside off, Shikhar looks to defend but his bottom hand comes off the bat. It is a jarring effect.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.

An appeal for a catch, turned down. Nothing in it. A length ball outside off, Dhawan looks to work it to the leg side but misses. The ball goes off the thigh pad to the keeper and the slip cordon goes up but the umpire is unmoved.
Looks to work it away but misses and is hit on the pads.

The physio is out in the middle again, with a big smile on his face. It is never a good feeling when you get hit on the same area twice but Dhawan manages a smile too. He gets his left thumb taped and is ready to go again. Fantastic commitment.

OUCH! Bang onto the gloves again! Almost a deja vu of the hit in the first over. This one landed around off and Dhawan looked to defend but the ball jagged back in, bounced and hit Dhawan on the left thumb. He throws his bat down and walks away to absorb the pain. Once again, Boult looks to sledge but his competitor is not even facing him.
EDGED, FOUR! Landed outside off, Vijay pushes forward and gets a thick outside edge which goes past gully to third man!
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On middle, pushed towards mid on.
Landed outside off, left alone.

Good shape to start. Full and outside off, swinging away, Vijay shoulders arms. It was that kind of a delivery which was the undoing of Vijay in the first innings. That came back in and bounced as well as opposed to this one.
MATT HENRY to share the new ball.
Good shape into the left hander, full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Landed outside off, played towards point.
Full and outside off, swinging away, too wide to be played at.
Landed outside off, left alone.

The physio is out in the middle. The magic spray comes out and it is sprayed in the area around the thumb and forefinger. The physio has a quiet word with Dhawan and then runs off. The thumb has swollen to a big extent but the fighter that he is, Dhawan is ready to play.

OUCH! That is a snorter! Pitched on a good length around middle, Dhawan looks to defend but the ball bounces sharply and hits Dhawan flush on the gloves. He immediately takes his gloves off and is in pain. Boult looks to sledge the batsman but on seeing that his competitor is in pain, prefers to keep his mouth shut.
On a good length outside off, moving away a touch, good bounce, Dhawan shoulders arms.
